If you set this value to false, then the stream will not be reusable, which means that it can only be bound to one broadcast. Non-reusable streams differ from reusable streams in the following ways: - A non-reusable stream can only be bound to one broadcast. - A non-reusable stream might be deleted by an automated process after the broadcast ends. - The liveStreams.list method does not list non-reusable streams if you call the method and set the mine parameter to true. ## Playlist

`object` model on the `json` wire format.

A *playlist* resource represents a YouTube playlist. A playlist is a collection of videos that can be viewed sequentially and shared with other users. A playlist can contain up to 200 videos, and YouTube does not limit the number of playlists that each user creates. By default, playlists are publicly visible to other users, but playlists can be public or private. YouTube also uses playlists to identify special collections of videos for a channel, such as: - uploaded videos - favorite videos - positively rated (liked) videos - watch history - watch later To be more specific, these lists are associated with a channel, which is a collection of a person, group, or company's videos, playlists, and other YouTube information. You can retrieve the playlist IDs for each of these lists from the channel resource for a given channel. You can then use the playlistItems.list method to retrieve any of those lists. You can also add or remove items from those lists by calling the playlistItems.insert and playlistItems.delete methods.

| Field | Wire name | Type | Required | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `contentDetails` | `contentDetails` | `PlaylistContentDetails` | No | No | The contentDetails object contains information like video count. |
| `etag` | `etag` | `string` | No | No | Etag of this resource. |
| `id` | `id` | `string` | No | No | The ID that YouTube uses to uniquely identify the playlist. |
| `kind` | `kind` | `string` | No | No | Identifies what kind of resource this is. Value: the fixed string "youtube#playlist". |
| `localizations` | `localizations` | `Record<string, PlaylistLocalization>` | No | No | Localizations for different languages |
| `player` | `player` | `PlaylistPlayer` | No | No | The player object contains information that you would use to play the playlist in an embedded player. |
| `snippet` | `snippet` | `PlaylistSnippet` | No | No | The snippet object contains basic details about the playlist, such as its title and description. |
| `status` | `status` | `PlaylistStatus` | No | No | The status object contains status information for the playlist. |

## PlaylistItem

`object` model on the `json` wire format.

A *playlistItem* resource identifies another resource, such as a video, that is included in a playlist. In addition, the playlistItem resource contains details about the included resource that pertain specifically to how that resource is used in that playlist. YouTube uses playlists to identify special collections of videos for a channel, such as: - uploaded videos - favorite videos - positively rated (liked) videos - watch history - watch later To be more specific, these lists are associated with a channel, which is a collection of a person, group, or company's videos, playlists, and other YouTube information. You can retrieve the playlist IDs for each of these lists from the channel resource for a given channel. You can then use the playlistItems.list method to retrieve any of those lists. You can also add or remove items from those lists by calling the playlistItems.insert and playlistItems.delete methods. For example, if a user gives a positive rating to a video, you would insert that video into the liked videos playlist for that user's channel.

## SearchResult

`object` model on the `json` wire format.

A search result contains information about a YouTube video, channel, or playlist that matches the search parameters specified in an API request. While a search result points to a uniquely identifiable resource, like a video, it does not have its own persistent data.

| Field | Wire name | Type | Required | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `etag` | `etag` | `string` | No | No | Etag of this resource. |
| `id` | `id` | `ResourceId` | No | No | The id object contains information that can be used to uniquely identify the resource that matches the search request. |
| `kind` | `kind` | `string` | No | No | Identifies what kind of resource this is. Value: the fixed string "youtube#searchResult". |
| `snippet` | `snippet` | `SearchResultSnippet` | No | No | The snippet object contains basic details about a search result, such as its title or description. For example, if the search result is a video, then the title will be the video's title and the description will be the video's description. |

## SearchResultSnippet

`object` model on the `json` wire format.

Basic details about a search result, including title, description and thumbnails of the item referenced by the search result.

| Field | Wire name | Type | Required | Nullable | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `channelId` | `channelId` | `string` | No | No | The value that YouTube uses to uniquely identify the channel that published the resource that the search result identifies. |
| `channelTitle` | `channelTitle` | `string` | No | No | The title of the channel that published the resource that the search result identifies. |
| `description` | `description` | `string` | No | No | A description of the search result. |
| `liveBroadcastContent` | `liveBroadcastContent` | `"none" \| "upcoming" \| "live" \| "completed"` | No | No | It indicates if the resource (video or channel) has upcoming/active live broadcast content. Or it's "none" if there is not any upcoming/active live broadcasts. |
| `publishedAt` | `publishedAt` | `string<date-time>` | No | No | The creation date and time of the resource that the search result identifies. |
| `thumbnails` | `thumbnails` | `ThumbnailDetails` | No | No | A map of thumbnail images associated with the search result. For each object in the map, the key is the name of the thumbnail image, and the value is an object that contains other information about the thumbnail. |
| `title` | `title` | `string` | No | No | The title of the search result. |

## Subscription

`object` model on the `json` wire format.

A *subscription* resource contains information about a YouTube user subscription. A subscription notifies a user when new videos are added to a channel or when another user takes one of several actions on YouTube, such as uploading a video, rating a video, or commenting on a video.

| `id` | `id` | `string` | No | No | The ID that YouTube uses to uniquely identify the subscription. |
| `kind` | `kind` | `string` | No | No | Identifies what kind of resource this is. Value: the fixed string "youtube#subscription". |
| `snippet` | `snippet` | `SubscriptionSnippet` | No | No | The snippet object contains basic details about the subscription, including its title and the channel that the user subscribed to. |
| `subscriberSnippet` | `subscriberSnippet` | `SubscriptionSubscriberSnippet` | No | No | The subscriberSnippet object contains basic details about the subscriber. |
